deterministic.name: check-verifier-contract.py
deterministic.evidence: Manual source plus hash-verified raw synthetic observations confirm a shared-template defect. .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r3/task/tests/test.sh:36-37 sends TERM then performs an unbounded wait; :154-159 stops waiting after five seconds without ensuring old-group exit; :168-183 records a replacement PID and accepts any HTTP responder without checking the new PID. qc/runs/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/per-row-review/evidence/21/controlled-recheck/restart-retains-old-process/restart-observation.json has before/after PID 189 and helper exit 0; its app-restart.log shows replacement EADDRINUSE then ready=1. The slow-shutdown case likewise retains PID 82. controlled-recheck/cli-failure-ignores-signal/observation.json times out at 8.003s with zero reward preserved and app PID296 still answering. probe-v2.py uses a local RewardKit stub and unchanged canonical test.sh; these are orchestration observations, not model scores. Syntax, early-zero/trap, suite order and helper export do pass, but truthful restart and bounded completion do not.
deterministic.counterexample: A memory-only app that ignores SIGTERM can appear durable because restart reports success while the original process keeps serving; a normally durable app with a legitimate 30-second graceful shutdown can also receive false restart success followed by service loss. On grader failure, the TERM-resistant child leaves cleanup waiting without bound.
deterministic.suggested_fix: Escalate the protected shared harness defect to its owner; after explicit authorization, implement bounded TERM/KILL group cleanup, prove the old group exited and the replacement PID remains alive before accepting HTTP, then freeze a new candidate and rerun normal/resistant/slow-shutdown fixtures. Do not patch task scoring or waive this finding.
